Issue found: File starts with a byte-order mark, which breaks the first column name in some tools.
Action taken: Read as UTF-8 with BOM removed.

Issue found: Looked for nulls, duplicate rows and duplicate EmployeeNumber.
Action taken: None found in 1,470 rows. The dataset is already clean, so the work is mostly transformation.

Issue found: Checked text columns for stray spaces and mixed spellings.
Three columns hold a single value for every employee (EmployeeCount=1, Over18=Y, StandardHours=80).
Action taken: Dropped. They cannot explain differences between employees.

Issue found: DailyRate, HourlyRate and MonthlyRate are unrelated to MonthlyIncome (correlations DailyRate 0.01, HourlyRate -0.02, MonthlyRate 0.03), while MonthlyIncome tracks JobLevel closely.
Action taken: Kept in the file but not used anywhere in the dashboard. MonthlyIncome is used as the pay measure.

Issue found: Attrition is Yes/No text, which is awkward to sum or average.
Action taken: Added Left (1 = left, 0 = stayed) and OvertimeFlag (1/0). Original text columns kept for slicers.

Issue found: Survey and rating columns are stored as numbers 1 to 4 (or 1 to 5), which read as meaningless on a chart.
Action taken: Added a text label column for each (e.g. JobSatisfactionLabel). The number stays for sorting. Label meanings follow the dataset's published data dictionary: confirm against your copy of the task materials.

Issue found: Continuous columns (age, tenure, income, distance, years with manager) are too granular for group comparison.
Action taken: Added 5 band columns, each with a *Sort column so Power BI can order bands correctly (use Sort by column). Band edges were chosen to give groups of reasonable size. Income is in the dataset's currency, which is not stated.

Issue found: Cost questions need a yearly figure.
The dashboard needs a way to prioritise current employees for a retention conversation.
Action taken: Added six yes/no risk flags (overtime, frequent travel, no stock options, tenure of 2 years or less, entry level (JobLevel 1), any of job satisfaction / environment satisfaction / work-life balance rated 1) and RiskFlagCount (0 to 6). This is a transparent rule, not a fitted model. The flags were chosen after looking at this same data (the entry-level flag was added after a first version flagged many senior staff who almost never leave), so its apparent accuracy is optimistic and should be tested on new data before relying on it.
